Volume estimate from Norris (1994) applied only to event 106, not to the precursors, based on interpretation in text that the main event was much larger than what Norris calls "precursors". Norris gives just a range of 1-5 x 10^5 m3, best estimate is taken in the middle (3 x 10^5 m3)
Archived seismic data is cut off too early so durations and end times could not be measured, but we do know from Norris (1994) that the shaking lasted for 9 minutes on RCS for the main event (106).

Event 106 is what seems to be the biggest of at least four rock falls, as there was data from three rockfall-like signals in the minutes before this event (121,122,123). For data to have been saved from events in 1989, they must have triggered the earthquake detection algorithm since continuous data was not saved. There could have been more related rock falls that did not generate signals large enough to trigger the detection algorithm.

At larger source-station distances, the P and S waves can be differentiated for these events (though they are not clearly pickable in most cases), indicating that the sources were impulsive, likely rock falls.
